newsitem.title: SPAIN: France most visited destination in 1996 - study.
newsitem.headline: France most visited destination in 1996 - study.

text.p: France was the most visited destination in the world in 1996 but the United States was the top earner from international tourism, the World Tourism Organisation said on Tuesday.

According to preliminary results from a study, international tourism grew by 4.6 percent in terms of arrivals to 592 million and 7.6 percent in terms of earnings to $423.1 billion, excluding airfares.
The WTO said it forecast world tourism would continue to grow by four percent a year for the rest of the decade to reach 700 million international arrivals and over $600 billion by the year 2000.
Among individual countries, France held on to the number one position with 61.5 million arrivals in 1996, but slipped to number three in terms of receipts, collecting some $28.2 billion.
The United States clocked up $64.4 billion in international tourism receipts, a 5.3 percent increase on 1995 and was the second most visited country in the world with 44.8 million arrivals.
Spain showed the steadiest growth in 1996, jumping from number four to number two in tourism receipts which rose 12.2 percent from the previous year to $26.4 billion.
China also saw strong growth, moving up a notch to number five in terms of arrivals of 26.1 million and number nine in receipts which reached $10.5 billion.
"1996 was an excellent year for tourism," said WTO Secretary-General Francesco Frangialli in a statement.

"The sustained growth that we have seen since the beginning of this decade and the acceleration now underway proves that tourism is one of the world's most durable and dynamic economic sectors," he added.
The WTO said by the year 2010, international tourist arrivals would top one billion and revenues would reach $1.55 billion annually, nearly four times more than current earnings.
The fastest growing region in 1996 was the Middle East which rose by more than 10 percent in terms of arrivals to 15 million and 15 percent in terms of receipts to $8.2 billion.
But the most visited continent remained Europe with 347 million arrivals and $214.5 billion in receipts.
